To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

blood perfusion data can be used as an alternative to temperature data for infrared face recognition, and the performance of infrared face recognition by means of blood-perfusion data can be improved by means of a simple blood perfusion model.
the blood perfusions are more consistent in terms of ambient temperature and more robust for IR face recognition.
the facial blood perfusion data can improve the performance of IR face recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new IR face recognition algorithm based on blood perfusion data.
the development of an infrared face recognition system based on the blood perfusion model.
the blood perfusion model, the conversion method of the temperature data into the blood perfusion one, and the performance of IR face recognition by using the blood perfusion information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method can improve the robustness of IR face recognition against ambient temperature variation.
the blood perfusions of human faces are a promising and effective way for infrared face recognition.
our blood perfusion model and blood perfusion-based face recognition method can be used to improve the recognition rate of IR face recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed blood perfusion model is effective in compensating for the effect of ambient temperature and thus improving the performance of IR face recognition.

we have developed a blood perfusion based face recognition algorithm which has been tested by using real data and the results have shown that the performance is superior to the conventional one by means of temperature data.
the blood perfusing model of faces based on thermodynamic theory and thermal physiology could be a feasible method to improve the IR face recognition performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermal physiology of human faces can be used to improve IR face recognition.
the facial blood perfusion data can be used as a new kind of feature for IR face recognition.
